content.title: Red Sox World Series Champion Pitcher Starting For Venezuela In WBC Final | NESN
content.text: The Boston Red Sox will have some stars playing in the World Baseball Classic Final, but a member of their 2018 World Series team will also be playing.When the United States batters step to the plate in the first inning, they will face former Red Sox pitcher Eduardo Rodriguez. The Red Sox traded for Rodriguez in 2014 in exchange for Andrew Miller. He made his debut with the team in 2015. As a rookie, he made 21 starts, posting a 3.85 ERA and striking out 98. From 2015-2021, Rodriguez started 153 games for the Red Sox and made six relief appearances in the regular season. He had a 4.16 ERA and 892 strikeouts. He appeared in 11 postseason games for the Red Sox as well.During the Red Sox's 2018 World Series run, Rodriguez pitched 10 postseason innings, making one start in seven games. He struck out 11 batters, but allowed seven earned runs. In the World Baseball Classic, he has made one start and allowed three earned runs in 2 2/3 innings of work.Venezuela has Wilyer Abreu and Willson Contreras on their team, while the United States has Roman Anthony and Garrett Whitlock. Regardless of which team wins, a couple of Red Sox players will be champions. Rodriguez has pitched in three World Series games and has allowed four earned runs in 6 1/3 innings of work.The World Baseball Classic will be pressure-filled, but Rodriguez has pitched on big stages before.More MLB: Why Caleb Durbin Trade Will End Up Being Best Move Red Sox Made This Offseason
